results.title: What's Your Angle?
results.brief_description:
A 2-player cooperative puzzle-platformer with a unique twist: asymmetrical gameplay. Unlike typical co-op games where players have similar roles, here each player experiences the game from a different gravity direction and faces unique obstacles. Despite their differences, both players contribute equally to solving the puzzles.
Each character has a unique gravity (e.g., one sees the world top-down, the other as a side-view platformer), creating drastically different experiences in the same level layout.
Players must collaborate, using character-specific abilities to assist each other and solve puzzles.
Unlike games like Toodee and Topdee, which split the perspectives, this game lets both gravity perspectives exist at the same time, adding complexity and creativity to the puzzles.

results.title: The Woods
results.credit_line:
Candice Breitz
Multi-channel installation, video, colour and audio
Commissioned by ACMI + PEM (Salem)
results.material_description: Multi-channel installation, video, colour and audio
results.brief_description: The Woods is a video installation comprised of three documentaries on child film stars from the United States of America, Nigeria and India. ‘The Audition’ features Hollywood stars, ‘The Interview’ features Nollywood stars, and ‘The Rehearsal’ features Bollywood stars. The Woods was exhibited at ACMI as part of The Character exhibition in 2015.

results.title: Cornflakes for tea
results.creator_credit: John Colquhoun, Tom Broadbridge and Andromeda Productions
results.brief_description: Dramatization of how a family living in high-rise inner city flats manage to cope with caring for each other when first their mother and then their father abandon them. Provides many points which could act as stimulus for discussion including perspectives on family relationships, contrasts on single parent and conventional nuclear families, welfare workers and their role, supportive community members, and the warm relationship of the central characters.

results.title: Oranges and lemons
results.creator_credit: Margot Lethlean and Swinburne Institute of Technology. Film and Television School
results.brief_description: A documentary on the early education of aboriginal children. It looks at a special pre-school program to help prepare aboriginal children for school, which has been set up in Dareton, Victoria. It suggests that in the face of insensitive attitudes, conventional education will further undermine aboriginal culture.

results.title: Loop
results.creator_credit: R. Barrington Scott and Southern Films
results.brief_description: A documentary about Melbourne’s Underground Rail Loop, its effect on the entire metropolitan railway system, and on the future of public transport in Melbourne. Shows the route the loop tracks and tunnels will follow around the city, the sites for the three new underground stations to supplement the present two stations, how passengers will travel from suburban stations when the loop is operating, how the loop is being constructed, and the benefits for train travellers of having five city stations close to shops, theatres and offices. Photographed by Volk Mol, sound by Don Boardman, edited by Geoff Wright, narrated by Michael Pate. Produced for the Melbourne Underground Rail Loop Authority.
